findings.title: die_model='distributed' decks are rejected by FastHenry (segments use nodes defined later in the file)
findings.detail: In the distributed branch, each footprint cell's die-top node `Nd…`, its column `Ev…` and its lateral segments `Edx/Edy…` are written together, in sorted cell order. Each lateral segment therefore names the +x or +y neighbour node before that node's line appears. FastHenry 3.0wr reads decks in a single pass and refuses any segment whose node it has not read yet. So both F6 die-model decks (point and tab terminals) cannot be read at all, and the F6 die variant in the claim does not work. The test `test_f6_variants_are_well_formed_together` only checks that every referenced node exists somewhere in the deck, not that it was defined first, so it passes on a broken deck. The fix is to emit all `Nd` node lines for a die before its `Ev`/`Ed` segments.
findings.evidence: I generated Case 4 base decks at FHLevel(cell_mm=1, plane_cell_mm=4, nh=1, wire_n=1) and ran the provisioned FastHenry (`-s iterative -m multi`). distributed_point and distributed_tab both exit with rc=1 and print 'No node read in yet named nd0i29y32 …'. In the deck, line 9917 `Edx0i28y32 Nd0i28y32 Nd0i29y32` comes before line 9938 `Nd0i29y32 x=…`. An order-aware scan counts 152 forward references for each distributed deck, i.e. every lateral die-top segment (4 dies × 38), and 0 for the short-die decks. Moving all node lines first in a scratch copy makes the distributed_point deck solve: rc=0, L=26.92 nH vs 25.57 nH for the short model. So ordering is the only defect, and it is real.
findings.suggested_check: Add a test that walks the deck in order and fails if any `E…` segment, `.equiv` or `.external` names a node not yet defined; ideally also run FastHenry on one coarse distributed deck when the binary is present.

findings.title: Lateral die-block segments are centred on the die top surface, so half of the block sits above the die
findings.detail: The `Ed` segments run between die-top nodes at z = DieShort.z_top with h = z_top - z_bottom. FastHenry centres a segment's cross-section on its node line, so the lateral block occupies [z_top - tb/2, z_top + tb/2]. The die itself occupies [z_bottom, z_top]. The module docstring lists the mesh's coarseness caveats (column overlaps, double-counted volume) but not this tb/2 vertical offset. The size of the effect is small but unmeasured. It affects only the non-verdict F6 diagnostic.
findings.evidence: Case 4: top-Cu top 2.236 mm, die z_bottom/z_top 2.236/2.416 mm, tb = 0.18 mm. The deck puts the Ed segments at z = 2.416 mm with h = 0.18 mm, so they span 2.326–2.506 mm, 0.09 mm of it above the die top.
findings.suggested_check: Place the lateral die-block nodes at (z_bottom+z_top)/2, or state the offset in the docstring.

findings.title: Tab-terminal deck at plane_cell_mm=4 crashes FastHenry's multipole solver
findings.detail: The tab deck is valid FastHenry input: the direct solver solves it, and multipole solves it at plane_cell_mm=2. At plane_cell_mm=4, though, the 2 mm posts enlarge the z-extent of the multipole partition. FastHenry then warns 'DivideSegs: tried to divide an indivisable segment' (a 4.1 mm plane segment against a 3.47 mm allowed length) and segfaults while building the preconditioner. This is a FastHenry robustness limit, not a deck error. Still, combining terminal_model='tab' with a 4 mm plane pitch under multipole is not usable, and the facts dict gives no warning.
findings.evidence: short_tab, plane 4 mm, multipole: rc=-11 after the DivideSegs warning. Direct solver: rc=0, 25.858 nH. Plane 2 mm, multipole: rc=0, Z=0.00817+1.60943j at 10 MHz (25.61 nH), vs short_point at the same level 25.53 nH.
findings.suggested_check: Document that tab decks need plane_cell_mm ≤ 2 mm (or the direct solver) under multipole, or run the tab variant in a smoke test.

findings.title: Wire ends on a die are snapped to a trace cell, unlike l2_layout
findings.detail: l2_layout's end_contact sends a wire end that lands on a die top to that die's merged node. The exporter always joins wire ends to the nearest trace cell of the wire's net. A layout with die-to-die stitching wires would silently get a different topology. The exporter does raise ValueError for wires that do not start on a die pad, but there is no matching guard for ends on a die. This is latent: none of 20 generated layouts (seeds 0–4, 2–3 dies per switch, 270 wires) has such a wire.
findings.evidence: Scan of `generate_layouts` output: 0 wire ends inside a die footprint, 0 exactly vertical wire segments.
findings.suggested_check: Raise ValueError (or route to the die node) when a wire end lies on a die footprint.

findings.title: Default models and parse_zc verified against the real binary
findings.detail: The default deck (short dies, point terminals) is read and solved by FastHenry 3.0wr. Both frequencies, 1e7 and 2e7, appear in Zc.mat, which confirms the ndec trick. parse_zc reads the real Zc.mat format correctly. The filament count FastHenry reports for the tab deck (8362) equals facts['n_filaments']. The equal-GMD square side 0.7788/(2·0.44705) = 0.87104 d checks out against Grover's g.m.d. values.
findings.evidence: short_point (plane 4 mm, multipole): rc=0, R=8.19 mΩ, L=25.568 nH at 10 and 20 MHz. short_point (plane 2 mm): Z = 0.00820323+1.60409j at 1e7, parsed correctly.

independent_checks_performed: Ran `uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_fasthenry.py` (24 passed) and `uv run ruff check` on both deliverables (clean).

Exported Case 4 base decks for all four combinations of die_model and terminal_model and ran the provisioned FastHenry 3.0wr binary on each (multipole), plus the direct solver on the tab deck and multipole at plane_cell_mm=2.
Order-aware scan of each deck for segment node references made before the node is defined: 152 in each distributed deck, 0 in each short-die deck.
Rebuilt the distributed deck with node lines first and solved it (26.92 nH vs 25.57 nH for the short model), showing ordering is the only defect.
Checked the Case 4 stack z-values (top Cu, die z_bottom/z_top) against the z-placement of the die-block segments.
Compared the die footprint, wire-end and contact rules with l2_layout.build_layout_system; scanned 20 generated layouts for wire ends on dies and vertical wire segments (none).
Parsed a real FastHenry Zc.mat with parse_zc and cross-checked facts['n_filaments'] against the filament count FastHenry reports.
caveats: FastHenry was run only on Case 4 base at a thin, coarse level (nh=1, wire_n=1, cell 1 mm). A run on a generated layout at cell 0.5 mm hit the background time limit and was stopped before finishing, so I cannot say whether default decks for generated layouts solve. I did not restart it because it does not affect the blocker.

I did not compare refinement convergence or FastHenry against l2_layout (no refinement level is frozen in this deliverable). The blocker concerns whether the decks are valid input, not the physics of the variants.
